```plaintext
        const nsWindow_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend4(@ptrCast(window), initSel, contentRect, styleMask, backingType, shouldDefer);
        // Assert: init must succeed.
        if (nsWindow_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSWindow initWithContentRect returned NULL. Window: {*}, selector: {*}, rect: {{x={d}, y={d}, w={d}, h={d}}}, styleMask={d}, backing={d}, defer={}", .{ window, initSel, contentRect.origin.x, contentRect.origin.y, contentRect.size.width, contentRect.size.height, styleMask, backingType, shouldDefer });
        }
        std.debug.assert(nsWindow_opt != null);
        const nsWindow: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsWindow_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(nsWindow) != 0);
        
        // Set window title: convert Zig string to NSString.
        const titleStr = try self.titleToNSString();
        // Assert: NSString creation must succeed.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(titleStr) != 0);
        defer {
            const releaseSel = c.sel_getUid("release");
            // Assert: selector must be valid.
            std.debug.assert(releaseSel != null);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(titleStr), releaseSel);
        }
        const setTitleSel = c.sel_getUid("setTitle:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (setTitleSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("setTitle: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(setTitleSel != null);
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(nsWindow), setTitleSel, titleStr);
        
        // Create NSView: single pointer to view object.
        const NSViewClass = c.objc_getClass("NSView");
        // Assert: NSView class must be available.
        if (NSViewClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView class not found. objc_getClass(\"NSView\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(NSViewClass != null);
        const view_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSViewClass), allocSel);
        // Assert: alloc must succeed.
        if (view_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView alloc returned NULL. Class: {*}, selector: {*}", .{ NSViewClass, allocSel });
        }
        std.debug.assert(view_opt != null);
        const view: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(view_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(view) != 0);
        const viewInitSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithFrame:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (viewInitSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("initWithFrame: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(viewInitSel != null);
        const nsView_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend1(@ptrCast(view), viewInitSel, contentRect);
        // Assert: init must succeed.
        if (nsView_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView initWithFrame returned NULL. View: {*}, selector: {*}, rect: {{x={d}, y={d}, w={d}, h={d}}}", .{ view, viewInitSel, contentRect.origin.x, contentRect.origin.y, contentRect.size.width, contentRect.size.height });
        }
        std.debug.assert(nsView_opt != null);
        const nsView: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsView_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(nsView) != 0);
        
        // Enable layer-backed view BEFORE setting as content view.
        // This ensures the layer is created and ready for Core Graphics drawing.
        const setWantsLayerSel = c.sel_getUid("setWantsLayer:");
        if (setWantsLayerSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("setWantsLayer: selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoidBool(@ptrCast(nsView), setWantsLayerSel, true);
        std.debug.print("[window] Enabled layer-backed view.\n", .{});
        
        // Set view as content view: single pointer assignment.
        const setContentViewSel = c.sel_getUid("setContentView:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(nsWindow), setContentViewSel, nsView);
        
        // Note: Layer will be created lazily when first accessed.
        // We'll access it in present() after the window is shown.
        
        // Store pointers: single-level only.
        self.ns_window = nsWindow;
        self.ns_view = nsView;
        self.ns_app = sharedApp;
        
        // Show window: makeKeyAndOrderFront.
        const makeKeySel = c.sel_getUid("makeKeyAndOrderFront:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(nsWindow), makeKeySel);
        
        // Activate application: bring to front.
        const activateSel = c.sel_getUid("activateIgnoringOtherApps:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoidBool(@ptrCast(sharedApp), activateSel, true);
        
        // Assert postcondition: window and view must be set.
        // Assert: ns_window and ns_view are non-optional pointers, so we just acknowledge their existence.
        _ = self.ns_window;
        _ = self.ns_view;
    }
    
    /// Convert Zig string to NSString: returns single pointer to NSString.
    /// Why: Cocoa APIs require NSString; we create it explicitly, caller releases.
    fn titleToNSString(self: *const Self) !*c.objc_object {
        const NSStringClass = c.objc_getClass("NSString");
        std.debug.assert(NSStringClass != null);
        const stringWithUTF8StringSel = c.sel_getUid("stringWithUTF8String:");
        // Create null-terminated C string from Zig slice.
        var title_buf: [256]u8 = undefined;
        std.debug.assert(self.title.len < title_buf.len);
        @memcpy(title_buf[0..self.title.len], self.title);
        title_buf[self.title.len] = 0;
        const nsString_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSendNSString(@ptrCast(NSStringClass), stringWithUTF8StringSel, &title_buf);
        std.debug.assert(nsString_opt != null);
        const nsString: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsString_opt.?));
        return nsString;
    }

    pub fn writePixels(self: *Self, pixels: []const u8) !void {
        // Assert arguments: pixels must be RGBA-aligned.
        std.debug.assert(pixels.len % 4 == 0);
        const max_size = self.width * self.height * 4;
        std.debug.assert(max_size > 0);
        std.debug.assert(max_size % 4 == 0);
        // Assert negative space: pixels must not exceed buffer.
        if (pixels.len > max_size) return error.BufferTooLarge;
        std.debug.assert(pixels.len <= max_size);
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be large enough.
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len >= pixels.len);
        @memcpy(self.rgba_buffer[0..pixels.len], pixels);
    }

    pub fn getBuffer(self: *Self) []u8 {
        // Assert precondition: self pointer must be valid.
        const self_ptr = @intFromPtr(self);
        if (self_ptr == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: self pointer is NULL", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self_ptr != 0);
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be initialized.
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: rgba_buffer is empty", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 != 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: rgba_buffer length ({d}) is not divisible by 4", .{self.rgba_buffer.len});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 == 0);
        const expected_size = @as(usize, self.width) * @as(usize, self.height) * 4;
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len != expected_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_size, self.rgba_buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len == expected_size);
        // Return slice of static buffer: use & to get pointer to array.
        return &self.rgba_buffer;
    }

    /// Present macOS window: draw RGBA buffer to view using Core Graphics.
    /// Why: NSView needs explicit drawing - we use Core Graphics to create CGImage and draw it.
    /// 
    /// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
    /// - `self: *Self`: Single pointer to Window struct.
    /// - `self.ns_view`: Single pointer to NSView (nullable).
    /// - `self.rgba_buffer`: Static buffer containing RGBA pixels.
    pub fn present(self: *Self) !void {
        // Assert precondition: view must be initialized.
        if (self.ns_view == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: ns_view is NULL. Call show() first.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.ns_view != null);
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        
        const view = self.ns_view.?;
        std.debug.print("[window] Presenting buffer to view at: 0x{x}, buffer size: {d} bytes\n", .{ @intFromPtr(view), self.rgba_buffer.len });
        
        // Get the view's layer (should already be created since we set wantsLayer in show()).
        const layerSel = c.sel_getUid("layer");
        if (layerSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: layer selector not found", .{});
        }
        var layer_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(view), layerSel);
        
        // If layer is NULL, try makeBackingLayer to create it.
        if (layer_opt == null) {
            std.debug.print("[window] view.layer is NULL, trying makeBackingLayer...\n", .{});
            const makeBackingLayerSel = c.sel_getUid("makeBackingLayer");
            if (makeBackingLayerSel == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.present: makeBackingLayer selector not found", .{});
            }
            layer_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(view), makeBackingLayerSel);
            if (layer_opt == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.present: makeBackingLayer returned NULL", .{});
            }
            std.debug.print("[window] Created layer via makeBackingLayer at: 0x{x}\n", .{@intFromPtr(layer_opt)});
        }
        
        if (layer_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: view.layer returned NULL after makeBackingLayer attempt", .{});
        }
        const layer: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(layer_opt.?));
        const layer_ptr_value = @intFromPtr(layer);
        if (layer_ptr_value == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: layer pointer is NULL after unwrap", .{});
        }
        if (layer_ptr_value < 0x1000) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: layer pointer is suspiciously small: 0x{x}", .{layer_ptr_value});
        }
        std.debug.print("[window] Got layer at: 0x{x}\n", .{layer_ptr_value});
        
        // Create CGImage from RGBA buffer using Core Graphics.
        // We'll use a C helper function to create the CGImage and set it as layer contents.
        // Note: rgba_buffer is an array, so we need & to get a slice.
        const cg_image = try createCGImageFromBuffer(&self.rgba_buffer, self.width, self.height);
        defer releaseCGImage(cg_image);
        
        // Set the CGImage as the layer's contents.
        const setContentsSel = c.sel_getUid("setContents:");
        if (setContentsSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: setContents: selector not found", .{});
        }
        // Note: setContents: expects an id, and CGImageRef is compatible.
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(layer), setContentsSel, @ptrCast(cg_image));
        
        // Mark layer as needing display.
        const setNeedsDisplaySel = c.sel_getUid("setNeedsDisplay");
        if (setNeedsDisplaySel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: setNeedsDisplay selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(layer), setNeedsDisplaySel);
        
        std.debug.print("[window] Set CGImage as layer contents and marked for display.\n", .{});
    }
    
    /// Create CGImage from RGBA buffer using Core Graphics.
    /// Returns: CGImageRef (opaque pointer).
    /// Note: Caller must call releaseCGImage when done.
    fn createCGImageFromBuffer(buffer: []const u8, width: u32, height: u32) !*anyopaque {
        std.debug.print("[window] Creating CGImage: {d}x{d}, buffer: {d} bytes\n", .{ width, height, buffer.len });
        
        // Assert: buffer must match dimensions.
        const expected_size = @as(usize, width) * @as(usize, height) * 4;
        if (buffer.len != expected_size) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_size, buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(buffer.len == expected_size);
        
        // Create CGColorSpace for RGB.
        const rgb_color_space = cg.CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB();
        if (rgb_color_space == null) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB returned NULL", .{});
        }
        defer cg.CGColorSpaceRelease(rgb_color_space);
        
        // Create CGDataProvider from our buffer.
        // Note: The buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of the image.
        // Since we're using a static buffer in the Window struct, this is safe.
        const data_provider = cg.CGDataProviderCreateWithData(
            null, // info pointer
            buffer.ptr, // data pointer
            buffer.len, // size
            null, // release callback (we manage memory ourselves)
        );
        if (data_provider == null) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: CGDataProviderCreateWithData returned NULL", .{});
        }
        defer cg.CGDataProviderRelease(data_provider);
        
        // Create CGImage from data provider.
        // Format: RGBA, 8 bits per component, 32 bits per pixel.
        // Note: kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast means RGBA format (alpha last).
        // kCGBitmapByteOrder32Big means big-endian byte order.
        const cg_image = cg.CGImageCreate(
            width, // width
            height, // height
            8, // bitsPerComponent
            32, // bitsPerPixel (8 bits * 4 components)
            width * 4, // bytesPerRow (RGBA = 4 bytes per pixel)
            rgb_color_space, // colorspace
            cg.kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast | cg.kCGBitmapByteOrder32Big, // bitmapInfo
            data_provider, // provider
            null, // decode array
            false, // shouldInterpolate
            cg.kCGRenderingIntentDefault, // intent
        );
        
        if (cg_image == null) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: CGImageCreate returned NULL", .{});
        }
        
        std.debug.print("[window] Created CGImage at: 0x{x}\n", .{@intFromPtr(cg_image)});
        return @ptrCast(cg_image);
    }
    
    /// Release CGImage.
    fn releaseCGImage(cg_image: *anyopaque) void {
        std.debug.print("[window] Releasing CGImage at: 0x{x}\n", .{@intFromPtr(cg_image)});
        cg.CGImageRelease(@ptrCast(cg_image));
    }
    
    /// Run NSApplication event loop: blocks until app terminates.
    /// Why: macOS apps need an event loop to process window events, keyboard input, etc.
    /// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
    /// - `self: *Self`: Single pointer to Window struct.
    /// - `self.ns_app`: Single pointer to NSApplication shared instance.
    pub fn runEventLoop(self: *Self) void {
        // Assert precondition: NSApplication must be initialized.
        std.debug.assert(self.ns_app != null);
        
        // Run event loop: blocks until app terminates.
        const runSel = c.sel_getUid("run");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(self.ns_app.?), runSel);
    }
};

```

`makeBackingLayer` also returns NULL. Switching to NSImage/NSBitmapImageRep to draw the buffer directly:


```plaintext
const std = @import("std");
const c = @import("objc_runtime.zig").c;
const cg = @import("objc_runtime.zig").cg;
const cocoa = @import("cocoa_bridge.zig");

/// Thin Cocoa bridge: Aurora owns the RGBA buffer; Cocoa just hosts the view.
/// ~<~ Glow Airbend: explicit allocations prevent dynamic Cocoa leaks into Zig runtime.
/// 
/// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
/// - `ns_window: ?*c.objc_object`: Single pointer to NSWindow (nullable for cleanup).
/// - `ns_view: ?*c.objc_object`: Single pointer to NSView (nullable for cleanup).
/// - `rgba_buffer: []u8`: Slice (single-level pointer to buffer).
/// - No double indirection: all pointers are single-level.
pub const Window = struct {
    title: []const u8,
    width: u32 = 1024,
    height: u32 = 768,
    /// Static buffer for RGBA pixels: avoids dynamic allocation.
    /// Size: 1024 * 768 * 4 = 3,145,728 bytes (3MB).
    /// Why: Static allocation eliminates allocator dependency and reduces runtime overhead.
    rgba_buffer: [1024 * 768 * 4]u8 = [_]u8{0} ** (1024 * 768 * 4),
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    /// Single pointer to NSWindow: nullable for cleanup safety.
    ns_window: ?*c.objc_object = null,
    /// Single pointer to NSView: nullable for cleanup safety.
    ns_view: ?*c.objc_object = null,
    /// Single pointer to NSApplication shared instance: nullable for cleanup safety.
    ns_app: ?*c.objc_object = null,

    const Self = @This();

    pub fn init(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, title: []const u8) !Window {
        // Assert arguments: title must not be empty and within bounds.
        if (title.len == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: title must not be empty", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(title.len > 0);
        if (title.len > 256) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: title length ({d}) exceeds maximum (256)", .{title.len});
        }
        std.debug.assert(title.len <= 256);
        // Assert compile-time constants: dimensions must be positive.
        const width: u32 = 1024;
        const height: u32 = 768;
        if (width == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: width must be positive", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(width > 0);
        if (height == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: height must be positive", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(height > 0);
        const buffer_size = width * height * 4;
        if (buffer_size == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: buffer_size must be positive", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(buffer_size > 0);
        if (buffer_size % 4 != 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: buffer_size ({d}) must be divisible by 4", .{buffer_size});
        }
        std.debug.assert(buffer_size % 4 == 0);
        // Assert: static buffer size matches calculated size.
        const static_buffer_size = @as(usize, width) * @as(usize, height) * 4;
        const buffer_type = @TypeOf((Window{ .title = title, .allocator = allocator }).rgba_buffer);
        if (@sizeOf(buffer_type) != static_buffer_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: static buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ static_buffer_size, @sizeOf(buffer_type) });
        }
        std.debug.assert(@sizeOf(buffer_type) == static_buffer_size);
        // Note: rgba_buffer is now statically allocated, no need for allocator.alloc.
        const window = Window{
            .title = title,
            .allocator = allocator,
            .rgba_buffer = [_]u8{0} ** (1024 * 768 * 4), // Initialize static buffer to zero.
        };
        // Assert postcondition: all fields must be initialized.
        if (window.title.len == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: title not initialized", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(window.title.len > 0);
        const actual_buffer_size = window.rgba_buffer.len;
        if (actual_buffer_size != buffer_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ buffer_size, actual_buffer_size });
        }
        std.debug.assert(actual_buffer_size == buffer_size);
        if (window.width != width) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: width mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ width, window.width });
        }
        std.debug.assert(window.width == width);
        if (window.height != height) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: height mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ height, window.height });
        }
        std.debug.assert(window.height == height);
        std.debug.assert(window.height == 768);
        return window;
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Self) void {
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 == 0);
        // Assert: static buffer should match expected size.
        const expected_buffer_size = @as(usize, self.width) * @as(usize, self.height) * 4;
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len != expected_buffer_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_buffer_size, self.rgba_buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len == expected_buffer_size);
        
        // Release Cocoa objects: single pointers, explicit cleanup.
        // Assert: ns_view pointer must be valid if not null.
        if (self.ns_view) |view| {
            const viewPtrValue = @intFromPtr(view);
            if (viewPtrValue == 0) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: ns_view pointer is NULL", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(viewPtrValue != 0);
            const releaseSel = c.sel_getUid("release");
            if (releaseSel == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: release selector not found", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(releaseSel != null);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(view), releaseSel);
        }
        // Assert: ns_window pointer must be valid if not null.
        if (self.ns_window) |window| {
            const windowPtrValue = @intFromPtr(window);
            if (windowPtrValue == 0) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: ns_window pointer is NULL", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(windowPtrValue != 0);
            const closeSel = c.sel_getUid("close");
            const releaseSel = c.sel_getUid("release");
            if (closeSel == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: close selector not found", .{});
            }
            if (releaseSel == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: release selector not found", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(closeSel != null);
            std.debug.assert(releaseSel != null);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(window), closeSel);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(window), releaseSel);
        }
        
        // Note: rgba_buffer is statically allocated, no need to free.
        // Assert postcondition: struct is cleared.
        self.* = undefined;
    }

    /// Show macOS window: initialize NSApplication, create NSWindow and NSView.
    /// Why: Minimal Cocoa shim; Aurora owns RGBA buffer, Cocoa hosts the view.
    /// 
    /// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
    /// - `self: *Self`: Single pointer to Window struct.
    /// - `ns_window`, `ns_view`: Single pointers to Objective-C objects.
    /// - All Objective-C message sends use single-level pointers.
    pub fn show(self: *Self) !void {
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be initialized.
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len == self.width * self.height * 4);
        std.debug.assert(self.width > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.height > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.title.len > 0);
        
        // Initialize Objective-C runtime: ensure Foundation classes are loaded.
        // Calling objc_getClass on NSObject triggers class loading for Foundation framework.
        const NSObjectClass = c.objc_getClass("NSObject");
        // Assert: NSObject should always be available (it's the root class).
        if (NSObjectClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSObject class not found. Objective-C runtime is not initialized. objc_getClass(\"NSObject\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(NSObjectClass != null);
        const nsObjectPtrValue = @intFromPtr(NSObjectClass);
        if (nsObjectPtrValue < 0x1000) {
            std.debug.panic("NSObject class pointer is suspiciously small: 0x{x}. Runtime may not be initialized.", .{nsObjectPtrValue});
        }
        
        // Initialize NSApplication: shared application instance.
        // Single pointer to Class, single pointer returned from message send.
        // Note: objc_getClass may return NULL if class isn't loaded yet.
        // We need to ensure Foundation is initialized by calling objc_getClass multiple times
        // or by using objc_lookUpClass which doesn't require the class to be loaded.
        var NSApplicationClass = c.objc_getClass("NSApplication");
        // Assert: objc_getClass should return non-null if Foundation is linked.
        if (NSApplicationClass == null) {
            // Try objc_lookUpClass as fallback (doesn't load the class, just looks it up)
            NSApplicationClass = c.objc_lookUpClass("NSApplication");
            // Assert: if still NULL, Foundation framework isn't properly linked or initialized.
            if (NSApplicationClass == null) {
                std.debug.panic("NSApplication class not found. Ensure Foundation and AppKit frameworks are linked in build.zig. objc_getClass and objc_lookUpClass both returned NULL.", .{});
            }
        }
        // Assert: class pointer must be valid before use.
        std.debug.assert(NSApplicationClass != null);
        // Unwrap the optional to get the actual class pointer.
        const NSApplicationClassUnwrapped = NSApplicationClass.?;
        // Debug: verify class pointer value to help diagnose segfault.
        // Note: Address 0x10 suggests invalid pointer (very close to NULL).
        // Important: @intFromPtr on an optional gives the address of the optional wrapper,
        // not the actual pointer value. We need to unwrap first.
        const classPtrValue = @intFromPtr(NSApplicationClassUnwrapped);
        // Assert: class pointer must be reasonable (not NULL, not suspiciously small).
        if (classPtrValue == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication class pointer is NULL. objc_getClass returned NULL even after fallback.", .{});
        }
        if (classPtrValue < 0x1000) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication class pointer is suspiciously small: 0x{x}. This suggests objc_getClass returned an invalid pointer. NSObject pointer was: 0x{x}", .{ classPtrValue, nsObjectPtrValue });
        }
        // Assert: class pointer should be aligned (Objective-C classes are typically aligned).
        if (classPtrValue % 8 != 0) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication class pointer is not properly aligned: 0x{x}. Expected 8-byte alignment.", .{classPtrValue});
        }
        // Additional verification: check if selector system is working.
        const respondsToSel = c.sel_getUid("respondsToSelector:");
        if (respondsToSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Selector system not working. sel_getUid(\"respondsToSelector:\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(respondsToSel != null);
        
        // Verify class structure: check ISA pointer (first field of objc_class structure).
        // On arm64, the ISA pointer should be valid and point to the metaclass.
        // Note: We can't directly access struct fields from @cImport, but we can check
        // if the memory at the class pointer location looks valid.
        // For now, we rely on the C wrapper's ISA pointer validation.
        
        // Get selector for sharedApplication class method.
        const sharedAppSel = c.sel_getUid("sharedApplication");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (sharedAppSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("sharedApplication selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(sharedAppSel != null);
        
        // Call sharedApplication class method.
        // Assert: class and selector must be valid before calling objc_msgSend.
        // Note: NSApplicationClassUnwrapped is already unwrapped, so we can't compare to null.
        std.debug.assert(sharedAppSel != null);
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(NSApplicationClassUnwrapped) != 0);
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(sharedAppSel) != 0);
        // Cast class pointer to anyopaque for objc_msgSend wrapper.
        // Note: We've already unwrapped NSApplicationClass, so we can cast directly.
        const classPtrForMsgSend: *const anyopaque = @ptrCast(NSApplicationClassUnwrapped);
        // Assert: cast should preserve pointer value.
        const classPtrAfterCast = @intFromPtr(classPtrForMsgSend);
        if (classPtrAfterCast != classPtrValue) {
            std.debug.panic("Class pointer changed after @ptrCast: before=0x{x}, after=0x{x}", .{ classPtrValue, classPtrAfterCast });
        }
        std.debug.assert(classPtrAfterCast == classPtrValue);
        // Call objc_msgSend wrapper.
        // Note: The C wrapper validates the ISA pointer and returns NULL if invalid.
        const sharedApp_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(classPtrForMsgSend, sharedAppSel);
        // Assert: sharedApplication should return non-null NSApplication instance.
        // If NULL, the class structure is invalid (ISA pointer check failed).
        if (sharedApp_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication sharedApplication returned NULL. This suggests the class structure is invalid (ISA pointer check failed). Class pointer: 0x{x}, selector: 0x{x}. Ensure Foundation and AppKit frameworks are properly linked and the Objective-C runtime is initialized.", .{ classPtrValue, @intFromPtr(sharedAppSel) });
        }
        std.debug.assert(sharedApp_opt != null);
        const sharedApp: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(sharedApp_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(sharedApp) != 0);
        
        // Create NSWindow: single pointer to window object.
        const NSWindowClass = c.objc_getClass("NSWindow");
        // Assert: NSWindow class must be available.
        if (NSWindowClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSWindow class not found. objc_getClass(\"NSWindow\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(NSWindowClass != null);
        
        // Window content rect: use Cocoa bridge NSRect struct.
        // Assert: width and height must be positive and reasonable.
        std.debug.assert(self.width > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.height > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.width <= 16384);
        std.debug.assert(self.height <= 16384);
        const contentRect = cocoa.NSRect{
            .origin = .{ .x = 100, .y = 100 },
            .size = .{ .width = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.width)), .height = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.height)) },
        };
        // Assert: rect values must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(contentRect.size.width > 0);
        std.debug.assert(contentRect.size.height > 0);
        
        // Window style mask: NSTitledWindowMask (1) | NSClosableWindowMask (2) | NSMiniaturizableWindowMask (4) | NSResizableWindowMask (8) = 15.
        const styleMask: usize = 15;
        const backingType: usize = 2; // NSBackingStoreBuffered
        const shouldDefer: bool = false;
        
        // Create window: single pointer returned.
        const allocSel = c.sel_getUid("alloc");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (allocSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("alloc selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(allocSel != null);
        const window_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSWindowClass), allocSel);
        // Assert: alloc must succeed.
        if (window_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSWindow alloc returned NULL. Class: {*}, selector: {*}", .{ NSWindowClass, allocSel });
        }
        std.debug.assert(window_opt != null);
        const window: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(window_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(window) != 0);
        
        const initSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithContentRect:styleMask:backing:defer:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (initSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("initWithContentRect:styleMask:backing:defer: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(initSel != null);
        const nsWindow_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend4(@ptrCast(window), initSel, contentRect, styleMask, backingType, shouldDefer);
        // Assert: init must succeed.
        if (nsWindow_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSWindow initWithContentRect returned NULL. Window: {*}, selector: {*}, rect: {{x={d}, y={d}, w={d}, h={d}}}, styleMask={d}, backing={d}, defer={}", .{ window, initSel, contentRect.origin.x, contentRect.origin.y, contentRect.size.width, contentRect.size.height, styleMask, backingType, shouldDefer });
        }
        std.debug.assert(nsWindow_opt != null);
        const nsWindow: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsWindow_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(nsWindow) != 0);
        
        // Set window title: convert Zig string to NSString.
        const titleStr = try self.titleToNSString();
        // Assert: NSString creation must succeed.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(titleStr) != 0);
        defer {
            const releaseSel = c.sel_getUid("release");
            // Assert: selector must be valid.
            std.debug.assert(releaseSel != null);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(titleStr), releaseSel);
        }
        const setTitleSel = c.sel_getUid("setTitle:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (setTitleSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("setTitle: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(setTitleSel != null);
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(nsWindow), setTitleSel, titleStr);
        
        // Create NSView: single pointer to view object.
        const NSViewClass = c.objc_getClass("NSView");
        // Assert: NSView class must be available.
        if (NSViewClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView class not found. objc_getClass(\"NSView\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(NSViewClass != null);
        const view_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSViewClass), allocSel);
        // Assert: alloc must succeed.
        if (view_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView alloc returned NULL. Class: {*}, selector: {*}", .{ NSViewClass, allocSel });
        }
        std.debug.assert(view_opt != null);
        const view: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(view_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(view) != 0);
        const viewInitSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithFrame:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (viewInitSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("initWithFrame: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(viewInitSel != null);
        const nsView_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend1(@ptrCast(view), viewInitSel, contentRect);
        // Assert: init must succeed.
        if (nsView_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView initWithFrame returned NULL. View: {*}, selector: {*}, rect: {{x={d}, y={d}, w={d}, h={d}}}", .{ view, viewInitSel, contentRect.origin.x, contentRect.origin.y, contentRect.size.width, contentRect.size.height });
        }
        std.debug.assert(nsView_opt != null);
        const nsView: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsView_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(nsView) != 0);
        
        // Enable layer-backed view BEFORE setting as content view.
        // This ensures the layer is created and ready for Core Graphics drawing.
        const setWantsLayerSel = c.sel_getUid("setWantsLayer:");
        if (setWantsLayerSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("setWantsLayer: selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoidBool(@ptrCast(nsView), setWantsLayerSel, true);
        std.debug.print("[window] Enabled layer-backed view.\n", .{});
        
        // Set view as content view: single pointer assignment.
        const setContentViewSel = c.sel_getUid("setContentView:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(nsWindow), setContentViewSel, nsView);
        
        // Note: Layer will be created lazily when first accessed.
        // We'll access it in present() after the window is shown.
        
        // Store pointers: single-level only.
        self.ns_window = nsWindow;
        self.ns_view = nsView;
        self.ns_app = sharedApp;
        
        // Show window: makeKeyAndOrderFront.
        const makeKeySel = c.sel_getUid("makeKeyAndOrderFront:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(nsWindow), makeKeySel);
        
        // Activate application: bring to front.
        const activateSel = c.sel_getUid("activateIgnoringOtherApps:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoidBool(@ptrCast(sharedApp), activateSel, true);
        
        // Assert postcondition: window and view must be set.
        // Assert: ns_window and ns_view are non-optional pointers, so we just acknowledge their existence.
        _ = self.ns_window;
        _ = self.ns_view;
    }
    
    /// Convert Zig string to NSString: returns single pointer to NSString.
    /// Why: Cocoa APIs require NSString; we create it explicitly, caller releases.
    fn titleToNSString(self: *const Self) !*c.objc_object {
        const NSStringClass = c.objc_getClass("NSString");
        std.debug.assert(NSStringClass != null);
        const stringWithUTF8StringSel = c.sel_getUid("stringWithUTF8String:");
        // Create null-terminated C string from Zig slice.
        var title_buf: [256]u8 = undefined;
        std.debug.assert(self.title.len < title_buf.len);
        @memcpy(title_buf[0..self.title.len], self.title);
        title_buf[self.title.len] = 0;
        const nsString_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSendNSString(@ptrCast(NSStringClass), stringWithUTF8StringSel, &title_buf);
        std.debug.assert(nsString_opt != null);
        const nsString: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsString_opt.?));
        return nsString;
    }

    pub fn writePixels(self: *Self, pixels: []const u8) !void {
        // Assert arguments: pixels must be RGBA-aligned.
        std.debug.assert(pixels.len % 4 == 0);
        const max_size = self.width * self.height * 4;
        std.debug.assert(max_size > 0);
        std.debug.assert(max_size % 4 == 0);
        // Assert negative space: pixels must not exceed buffer.
        if (pixels.len > max_size) return error.BufferTooLarge;
        std.debug.assert(pixels.len <= max_size);
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be large enough.
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len >= pixels.len);
        @memcpy(self.rgba_buffer[0..pixels.len], pixels);
    }

    pub fn getBuffer(self: *Self) []u8 {
        // Assert precondition: self pointer must be valid.
        const self_ptr = @intFromPtr(self);
        if (self_ptr == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: self pointer is NULL", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self_ptr != 0);
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be initialized.
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: rgba_buffer is empty", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 != 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: rgba_buffer length ({d}) is not divisible by 4", .{self.rgba_buffer.len});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 == 0);
        const expected_size = @as(usize, self.width) * @as(usize, self.height) * 4;
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len != expected_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_size, self.rgba_buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len == expected_size);
        // Return slice of static buffer: use & to get pointer to array.
        return &self.rgba_buffer;
    }

    /// Present macOS window: draw RGBA buffer to view using NSBitmapImageRep and NSImage.
    /// Why: Simpler than layer-backed views - we create an NSImage from our buffer and draw it.
    /// 
    /// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
    /// - `self: *Self`: Single pointer to Window struct.
    /// - `self.ns_view`: Single pointer to NSView (nullable).
    /// - `self.rgba_buffer`: Static buffer containing RGBA pixels.
    pub fn present(self: *Self) !void {
        // Assert precondition: view must be initialized.
        if (self.ns_view == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: ns_view is NULL. Call show() first.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.ns_view != null);
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        
        const view = self.ns_view.?;
        std.debug.print("[window] Presenting buffer to view at: 0x{x}, buffer size: {d} bytes\n", .{ @intFromPtr(view), self.rgba_buffer.len });

        if (NSBitmapImageRepClass == null) {

            std.debug.panic("Window.present: alloc selector not found", .{});

        if (bitmapRep_alloc_opt == null) {

        // Initialize with bitmap data: initWithBitmapDataPlanes:pixelsWide:pixelsHigh:bitsPerSample:samplesPerPixel:hasAlpha:isPlanar:colorSpaceName:bytesPerRow:bitsPerPixel:
        // We'll use a simpler approach: create CGImage first, then convert to NSImage.
        const cg_image = try createCGImageFromBuffer(&self.rgba_buffer, self.width, self.height);
        defer releaseCGImage(cg_image);
        
        // Create NSImage from CGImage.
        const NSImageClass = c.objc_getClass("NSImage");
        if (NSImageClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSImage class not found", .{});
        }
        const nsImage_alloc_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSImageClass), allocSel);
        if (nsImage_alloc_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSImage alloc returned NULL", .{});
        }
        const nsImage_alloc: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsImage_alloc_opt.?));
        
        // Initialize NSImage with CGImage: initWithCGImage:size:
        const initSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithCGImage:size:");
        if (initSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: initWithCGImage:size: selector not found", .{});
        }
        // Create NSSize struct for image size.
        const NSSize = extern struct {
            width: f64,
            height: f64,
        };
        const image_size = NSSize{
            .width = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.width)),
            .height = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.height)),
        };
        const nsImage_init_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend1(@ptrCast(nsImage_alloc), initSel, &image_size);
        if (nsImage_init_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSImage initWithCGImage:size: returned NULL", .{});
        }

        std.debug.print("[window] Created NSImage at: 0x{x}\n", .{@intFromPtr(nsImage)});

        if (lockFocusSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: lockFocus selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(view), lockFocusSel);

        if (drawInRectSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: drawInRect:fromRect:operation:fraction: selector not found", .{});
        }

        const compositeSourceOver: c_int = 0;
        const fraction: f64 = 1.0;
        // We need a wrapper for this complex call. For now, use a simpler drawInRect:.
        const drawInRectSimpleSel = c.sel_getUid("drawInRect:");
        if (drawInRectSimpleSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: drawInRect: selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(nsImage), drawInRectSimpleSel, bounds);
        
        // Unlock focus.
        const unlockFocusSel = c.sel_getUid("unlockFocus");
        if (unlockFocusSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: unlockFocus selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(view), unlockFocusSel);
        
        // Mark view as needing display.
        const setNeedsDisplaySel = c.sel_getUid("setNeedsDisplay:");
        if (setNeedsDisplaySel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: setNeedsDisplay: selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoidBool(@ptrCast(view), setNeedsDisplaySel, true);
        
        std.debug.print("[window] Drew NSImage to view and marked for display.\n", .{});
    }
    
    /// Create CGImage from RGBA buffer using Core Graphics.
    /// Returns: CGImageRef (opaque pointer).
    /// Note: Caller must call releaseCGImage when done.
    fn createCGImageFromBuffer(buffer: []const u8, width: u32, height: u32) !*anyopaque {
        std.debug.print("[window] Creating CGImage: {d}x{d}, buffer: {d} bytes\n", .{ width, height, buffer.len });
        
        // Assert: buffer must match dimensions.
        const expected_size = @as(usize, width) * @as(usize, height) * 4;
        if (buffer.len != expected_size) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_size, buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(buffer.len == expected_size);
        
        // Create CGColorSpace for RGB.
        const rgb_color_space = cg.CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB();
        if (rgb_color_space == null) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB returned NULL", .{});
        }
        defer cg.CGColorSpaceRelease(rgb_color_space);
        
        // Create CGDataProvider from our buffer.
        // Note: The buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of the image.
        // Since we're using a static buffer in the Window struct, this is safe.
        const data_provider = cg.CGDataProviderCreateWithData(
            null, // info pointer
            buffer.ptr, // data pointer
            buffer.len, // size
            null, // release callback (we manage memory ourselves)
        );
        if (data_provider == null) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: CGDataProviderCreateWithData returned NULL", .{});
        }
        defer cg.CGDataProviderRelease(data_provider);
        
        // Create CGImage from data provider.
        // Format: RGBA, 8 bits per component, 32 bits per pixel.
        // Note: kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast means RGBA format (alpha last).
        // kCGBitmapByteOrder32Big means big-endian byte order.
        const cg_image = cg.CGImageCreate(
            width, // width
            height, // height
            8, // bitsPerComponent
            32, // bitsPerPixel (8 bits * 4 components)
            width * 4, // bytesPerRow (RGBA = 4 bytes per pixel)
            rgb_color_space, // colorspace
            cg.kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast | cg.kCGBitmapByteOrder32Big, // bitmapInfo
            data_provider, // provider
            null, // decode array
            false, // shouldInterpolate
            cg.kCGRenderingIntentDefault, // intent
        );
        
        if (cg_image == null) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: CGImageCreate returned NULL", .{});
        }
        
        std.debug.print("[window] Created CGImage at: 0x{x}\n", .{@intFromPtr(cg_image)});
        return @ptrCast(cg_image);
    }
    
    /// Release CGImage.
    fn releaseCGImage(cg_image: *anyopaque) void {
        std.debug.print("[window] Releasing CGImage at: 0x{x}\n", .{@intFromPtr(cg_image)});
        cg.CGImageRelease(@ptrCast(cg_image));
    }
    
    /// Run NSApplication event loop: blocks until app terminates.
    /// Why: macOS apps need an event loop to process window events, keyboard input, etc.
    /// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
    /// - `self: *Self`: Single pointer to Window struct.
    /// - `self.ns_app`: Single pointer to NSApplication shared instance.
    pub fn runEventLoop(self: *Self) void {
        // Assert precondition: NSApplication must be initialized.
        std.debug.assert(self.ns_app != null);
        
        // Run event loop: blocks until app terminates.
        const runSel = c.sel_getUid("run");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(self.ns_app.?), runSel);
    }
};

```

Adding a wrapper for `initWithCGImage:size:` and simplifying the approach. Checking what we need:


```plaintext
const std = @import("std");
const c = @import("objc_runtime.zig").c;
const cg = @import("objc_runtime.zig").cg;
const cocoa = @import("cocoa_bridge.zig");

/// Thin Cocoa bridge: Aurora owns the RGBA buffer; Cocoa just hosts the view.
/// ~<~ Glow Airbend: explicit allocations prevent dynamic Cocoa leaks into Zig runtime.
/// 
/// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
/// - `ns_window: ?*c.objc_object`: Single pointer to NSWindow (nullable for cleanup).
/// - `ns_view: ?*c.objc_object`: Single pointer to NSView (nullable for cleanup).
/// - `rgba_buffer: []u8`: Slice (single-level pointer to buffer).
/// - No double indirection: all pointers are single-level.
pub const Window = struct {
    title: []const u8,
    width: u32 = 1024,
    height: u32 = 768,
    /// Static buffer for RGBA pixels: avoids dynamic allocation.
    /// Size: 1024 * 768 * 4 = 3,145,728 bytes (3MB).
    /// Why: Static allocation eliminates allocator dependency and reduces runtime overhead.
    rgba_buffer: [1024 * 768 * 4]u8 = [_]u8{0} ** (1024 * 768 * 4),
    allocator: std.mem.Allocator,
    /// Single pointer to NSWindow: nullable for cleanup safety.
    ns_window: ?*c.objc_object = null,
    /// Single pointer to NSView: nullable for cleanup safety.
    ns_view: ?*c.objc_object = null,
    /// Single pointer to NSApplication shared instance: nullable for cleanup safety.
    ns_app: ?*c.objc_object = null,

    const Self = @This();

    pub fn init(allocator: std.mem.Allocator, title: []const u8) !Window {
        // Assert arguments: title must not be empty and within bounds.
        if (title.len == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: title must not be empty", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(title.len > 0);
        if (title.len > 256) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: title length ({d}) exceeds maximum (256)", .{title.len});
        }
        std.debug.assert(title.len <= 256);
        // Assert compile-time constants: dimensions must be positive.
        const width: u32 = 1024;
        const height: u32 = 768;
        if (width == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: width must be positive", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(width > 0);
        if (height == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: height must be positive", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(height > 0);
        const buffer_size = width * height * 4;
        if (buffer_size == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: buffer_size must be positive", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(buffer_size > 0);
        if (buffer_size % 4 != 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: buffer_size ({d}) must be divisible by 4", .{buffer_size});
        }
        std.debug.assert(buffer_size % 4 == 0);
        // Assert: static buffer size matches calculated size.
        const static_buffer_size = @as(usize, width) * @as(usize, height) * 4;
        const buffer_type = @TypeOf((Window{ .title = title, .allocator = allocator }).rgba_buffer);
        if (@sizeOf(buffer_type) != static_buffer_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: static buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ static_buffer_size, @sizeOf(buffer_type) });
        }
        std.debug.assert(@sizeOf(buffer_type) == static_buffer_size);
        // Note: rgba_buffer is now statically allocated, no need for allocator.alloc.
        const window = Window{
            .title = title,
            .allocator = allocator,
            .rgba_buffer = [_]u8{0} ** (1024 * 768 * 4), // Initialize static buffer to zero.
        };
        // Assert postcondition: all fields must be initialized.
        if (window.title.len == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: title not initialized", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(window.title.len > 0);
        const actual_buffer_size = window.rgba_buffer.len;
        if (actual_buffer_size != buffer_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ buffer_size, actual_buffer_size });
        }
        std.debug.assert(actual_buffer_size == buffer_size);
        if (window.width != width) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: width mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ width, window.width });
        }
        std.debug.assert(window.width == width);
        if (window.height != height) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.init: height mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ height, window.height });
        }
        std.debug.assert(window.height == height);
        std.debug.assert(window.height == 768);
        return window;
    }

    pub fn deinit(self: *Self) void {
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 == 0);
        // Assert: static buffer should match expected size.
        const expected_buffer_size = @as(usize, self.width) * @as(usize, self.height) * 4;
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len != expected_buffer_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_buffer_size, self.rgba_buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len == expected_buffer_size);
        
        // Release Cocoa objects: single pointers, explicit cleanup.
        // Assert: ns_view pointer must be valid if not null.
        if (self.ns_view) |view| {
            const viewPtrValue = @intFromPtr(view);
            if (viewPtrValue == 0) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: ns_view pointer is NULL", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(viewPtrValue != 0);
            const releaseSel = c.sel_getUid("release");
            if (releaseSel == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: release selector not found", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(releaseSel != null);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(view), releaseSel);
        }
        // Assert: ns_window pointer must be valid if not null.
        if (self.ns_window) |window| {
            const windowPtrValue = @intFromPtr(window);
            if (windowPtrValue == 0) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: ns_window pointer is NULL", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(windowPtrValue != 0);
            const closeSel = c.sel_getUid("close");
            const releaseSel = c.sel_getUid("release");
            if (closeSel == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: close selector not found", .{});
            }
            if (releaseSel == null) {
                std.debug.panic("Window.deinit: release selector not found", .{});
            }
            std.debug.assert(closeSel != null);
            std.debug.assert(releaseSel != null);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(window), closeSel);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(window), releaseSel);
        }
        
        // Note: rgba_buffer is statically allocated, no need to free.
        // Assert postcondition: struct is cleared.
        self.* = undefined;
    }

    /// Show macOS window: initialize NSApplication, create NSWindow and NSView.
    /// Why: Minimal Cocoa shim; Aurora owns RGBA buffer, Cocoa hosts the view.
    /// 
    /// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
    /// - `self: *Self`: Single pointer to Window struct.
    /// - `ns_window`, `ns_view`: Single pointers to Objective-C objects.
    /// - All Objective-C message sends use single-level pointers.
    pub fn show(self: *Self) !void {
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be initialized.
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len == self.width * self.height * 4);
        std.debug.assert(self.width > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.height > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.title.len > 0);
        
        // Initialize Objective-C runtime: ensure Foundation classes are loaded.
        // Calling objc_getClass on NSObject triggers class loading for Foundation framework.
        const NSObjectClass = c.objc_getClass("NSObject");
        // Assert: NSObject should always be available (it's the root class).
        if (NSObjectClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSObject class not found. Objective-C runtime is not initialized. objc_getClass(\"NSObject\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(NSObjectClass != null);
        const nsObjectPtrValue = @intFromPtr(NSObjectClass);
        if (nsObjectPtrValue < 0x1000) {
            std.debug.panic("NSObject class pointer is suspiciously small: 0x{x}. Runtime may not be initialized.", .{nsObjectPtrValue});
        }
        
        // Initialize NSApplication: shared application instance.
        // Single pointer to Class, single pointer returned from message send.
        // Note: objc_getClass may return NULL if class isn't loaded yet.
        // We need to ensure Foundation is initialized by calling objc_getClass multiple times
        // or by using objc_lookUpClass which doesn't require the class to be loaded.
        var NSApplicationClass = c.objc_getClass("NSApplication");
        // Assert: objc_getClass should return non-null if Foundation is linked.
        if (NSApplicationClass == null) {
            // Try objc_lookUpClass as fallback (doesn't load the class, just looks it up)
            NSApplicationClass = c.objc_lookUpClass("NSApplication");
            // Assert: if still NULL, Foundation framework isn't properly linked or initialized.
            if (NSApplicationClass == null) {
                std.debug.panic("NSApplication class not found. Ensure Foundation and AppKit frameworks are linked in build.zig. objc_getClass and objc_lookUpClass both returned NULL.", .{});
            }
        }
        // Assert: class pointer must be valid before use.
        std.debug.assert(NSApplicationClass != null);
        // Unwrap the optional to get the actual class pointer.
        const NSApplicationClassUnwrapped = NSApplicationClass.?;
        // Debug: verify class pointer value to help diagnose segfault.
        // Note: Address 0x10 suggests invalid pointer (very close to NULL).
        // Important: @intFromPtr on an optional gives the address of the optional wrapper,
        // not the actual pointer value. We need to unwrap first.
        const classPtrValue = @intFromPtr(NSApplicationClassUnwrapped);
        // Assert: class pointer must be reasonable (not NULL, not suspiciously small).
        if (classPtrValue == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication class pointer is NULL. objc_getClass returned NULL even after fallback.", .{});
        }
        if (classPtrValue < 0x1000) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication class pointer is suspiciously small: 0x{x}. This suggests objc_getClass returned an invalid pointer. NSObject pointer was: 0x{x}", .{ classPtrValue, nsObjectPtrValue });
        }
        // Assert: class pointer should be aligned (Objective-C classes are typically aligned).
        if (classPtrValue % 8 != 0) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication class pointer is not properly aligned: 0x{x}. Expected 8-byte alignment.", .{classPtrValue});
        }
        // Additional verification: check if selector system is working.
        const respondsToSel = c.sel_getUid("respondsToSelector:");
        if (respondsToSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Selector system not working. sel_getUid(\"respondsToSelector:\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(respondsToSel != null);
        
        // Verify class structure: check ISA pointer (first field of objc_class structure).
        // On arm64, the ISA pointer should be valid and point to the metaclass.
        // Note: We can't directly access struct fields from @cImport, but we can check
        // if the memory at the class pointer location looks valid.
        // For now, we rely on the C wrapper's ISA pointer validation.
        
        // Get selector for sharedApplication class method.
        const sharedAppSel = c.sel_getUid("sharedApplication");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (sharedAppSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("sharedApplication selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(sharedAppSel != null);
        
        // Call sharedApplication class method.
        // Assert: class and selector must be valid before calling objc_msgSend.
        // Note: NSApplicationClassUnwrapped is already unwrapped, so we can't compare to null.
        std.debug.assert(sharedAppSel != null);
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(NSApplicationClassUnwrapped) != 0);
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(sharedAppSel) != 0);
        // Cast class pointer to anyopaque for objc_msgSend wrapper.
        // Note: We've already unwrapped NSApplicationClass, so we can cast directly.
        const classPtrForMsgSend: *const anyopaque = @ptrCast(NSApplicationClassUnwrapped);
        // Assert: cast should preserve pointer value.
        const classPtrAfterCast = @intFromPtr(classPtrForMsgSend);
        if (classPtrAfterCast != classPtrValue) {
            std.debug.panic("Class pointer changed after @ptrCast: before=0x{x}, after=0x{x}", .{ classPtrValue, classPtrAfterCast });
        }
        std.debug.assert(classPtrAfterCast == classPtrValue);
        // Call objc_msgSend wrapper.
        // Note: The C wrapper validates the ISA pointer and returns NULL if invalid.
        const sharedApp_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(classPtrForMsgSend, sharedAppSel);
        // Assert: sharedApplication should return non-null NSApplication instance.
        // If NULL, the class structure is invalid (ISA pointer check failed).
        if (sharedApp_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSApplication sharedApplication returned NULL. This suggests the class structure is invalid (ISA pointer check failed). Class pointer: 0x{x}, selector: 0x{x}. Ensure Foundation and AppKit frameworks are properly linked and the Objective-C runtime is initialized.", .{ classPtrValue, @intFromPtr(sharedAppSel) });
        }
        std.debug.assert(sharedApp_opt != null);
        const sharedApp: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(sharedApp_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(sharedApp) != 0);
        
        // Create NSWindow: single pointer to window object.
        const NSWindowClass = c.objc_getClass("NSWindow");
        // Assert: NSWindow class must be available.
        if (NSWindowClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSWindow class not found. objc_getClass(\"NSWindow\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(NSWindowClass != null);
        
        // Window content rect: use Cocoa bridge NSRect struct.
        // Assert: width and height must be positive and reasonable.
        std.debug.assert(self.width > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.height > 0);
        std.debug.assert(self.width <= 16384);
        std.debug.assert(self.height <= 16384);
        const contentRect = cocoa.NSRect{
            .origin = .{ .x = 100, .y = 100 },
            .size = .{ .width = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.width)), .height = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.height)) },
        };
        // Assert: rect values must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(contentRect.size.width > 0);
        std.debug.assert(contentRect.size.height > 0);
        
        // Window style mask: NSTitledWindowMask (1) | NSClosableWindowMask (2) | NSMiniaturizableWindowMask (4) | NSResizableWindowMask (8) = 15.
        const styleMask: usize = 15;
        const backingType: usize = 2; // NSBackingStoreBuffered
        const shouldDefer: bool = false;
        
        // Create window: single pointer returned.
        const allocSel = c.sel_getUid("alloc");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (allocSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("alloc selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(allocSel != null);
        const window_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSWindowClass), allocSel);
        // Assert: alloc must succeed.
        if (window_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSWindow alloc returned NULL. Class: {*}, selector: {*}", .{ NSWindowClass, allocSel });
        }
        std.debug.assert(window_opt != null);
        const window: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(window_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(window) != 0);
        
        const initSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithContentRect:styleMask:backing:defer:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (initSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("initWithContentRect:styleMask:backing:defer: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(initSel != null);
        const nsWindow_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend4(@ptrCast(window), initSel, contentRect, styleMask, backingType, shouldDefer);
        // Assert: init must succeed.
        if (nsWindow_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSWindow initWithContentRect returned NULL. Window: {*}, selector: {*}, rect: {{x={d}, y={d}, w={d}, h={d}}}, styleMask={d}, backing={d}, defer={}", .{ window, initSel, contentRect.origin.x, contentRect.origin.y, contentRect.size.width, contentRect.size.height, styleMask, backingType, shouldDefer });
        }
        std.debug.assert(nsWindow_opt != null);
        const nsWindow: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsWindow_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(nsWindow) != 0);
        
        // Set window title: convert Zig string to NSString.
        const titleStr = try self.titleToNSString();
        // Assert: NSString creation must succeed.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(titleStr) != 0);
        defer {
            const releaseSel = c.sel_getUid("release");
            // Assert: selector must be valid.
            std.debug.assert(releaseSel != null);
            cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(titleStr), releaseSel);
        }
        const setTitleSel = c.sel_getUid("setTitle:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (setTitleSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("setTitle: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(setTitleSel != null);
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(nsWindow), setTitleSel, titleStr);
        
        // Create NSView: single pointer to view object.
        const NSViewClass = c.objc_getClass("NSView");
        // Assert: NSView class must be available.
        if (NSViewClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView class not found. objc_getClass(\"NSView\") returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(NSViewClass != null);
        const view_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSViewClass), allocSel);
        // Assert: alloc must succeed.
        if (view_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView alloc returned NULL. Class: {*}, selector: {*}", .{ NSViewClass, allocSel });
        }
        std.debug.assert(view_opt != null);
        const view: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(view_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(view) != 0);
        const viewInitSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithFrame:");
        // Assert: selector must be valid.
        if (viewInitSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("initWithFrame: selector not found. sel_getUid returned NULL.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(viewInitSel != null);
        const nsView_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend1(@ptrCast(view), viewInitSel, contentRect);
        // Assert: init must succeed.
        if (nsView_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("NSView initWithFrame returned NULL. View: {*}, selector: {*}, rect: {{x={d}, y={d}, w={d}, h={d}}}", .{ view, viewInitSel, contentRect.origin.x, contentRect.origin.y, contentRect.size.width, contentRect.size.height });
        }
        std.debug.assert(nsView_opt != null);
        const nsView: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsView_opt.?));
        // Assert: unwrapped pointer must be valid.
        std.debug.assert(@intFromPtr(nsView) != 0);
        
        // Enable layer-backed view BEFORE setting as content view.
        // This ensures the layer is created and ready for Core Graphics drawing.
        const setWantsLayerSel = c.sel_getUid("setWantsLayer:");
        if (setWantsLayerSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("setWantsLayer: selector not found", .{});
        }
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoidBool(@ptrCast(nsView), setWantsLayerSel, true);
        std.debug.print("[window] Enabled layer-backed view.\n", .{});
        
        // Set view as content view: single pointer assignment.
        const setContentViewSel = c.sel_getUid("setContentView:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid1(@ptrCast(nsWindow), setContentViewSel, nsView);
        
        // Note: Layer will be created lazily when first accessed.
        // We'll access it in present() after the window is shown.
        
        // Store pointers: single-level only.
        self.ns_window = nsWindow;
        self.ns_view = nsView;
        self.ns_app = sharedApp;
        
        // Show window: makeKeyAndOrderFront.
        const makeKeySel = c.sel_getUid("makeKeyAndOrderFront:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoid0(@ptrCast(nsWindow), makeKeySel);
        
        // Activate application: bring to front.
        const activateSel = c.sel_getUid("activateIgnoringOtherApps:");
        cocoa.objc_msgSendVoidBool(@ptrCast(sharedApp), activateSel, true);
        
        // Assert postcondition: window and view must be set.
        // Assert: ns_window and ns_view are non-optional pointers, so we just acknowledge their existence.
        _ = self.ns_window;
        _ = self.ns_view;
    }
    
    /// Convert Zig string to NSString: returns single pointer to NSString.
    /// Why: Cocoa APIs require NSString; we create it explicitly, caller releases.
    fn titleToNSString(self: *const Self) !*c.objc_object {
        const NSStringClass = c.objc_getClass("NSString");
        std.debug.assert(NSStringClass != null);
        const stringWithUTF8StringSel = c.sel_getUid("stringWithUTF8String:");
        // Create null-terminated C string from Zig slice.
        var title_buf: [256]u8 = undefined;
        std.debug.assert(self.title.len < title_buf.len);
        @memcpy(title_buf[0..self.title.len], self.title);
        title_buf[self.title.len] = 0;
        const nsString_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSendNSString(@ptrCast(NSStringClass), stringWithUTF8StringSel, &title_buf);
        std.debug.assert(nsString_opt != null);
        const nsString: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsString_opt.?));
        return nsString;
    }

    pub fn writePixels(self: *Self, pixels: []const u8) !void {
        // Assert arguments: pixels must be RGBA-aligned.
        std.debug.assert(pixels.len % 4 == 0);
        const max_size = self.width * self.height * 4;
        std.debug.assert(max_size > 0);
        std.debug.assert(max_size % 4 == 0);
        // Assert negative space: pixels must not exceed buffer.
        if (pixels.len > max_size) return error.BufferTooLarge;
        std.debug.assert(pixels.len <= max_size);
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be large enough.
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len >= pixels.len);
        @memcpy(self.rgba_buffer[0..pixels.len], pixels);
    }

    pub fn getBuffer(self: *Self) []u8 {
        // Assert precondition: self pointer must be valid.
        const self_ptr = @intFromPtr(self);
        if (self_ptr == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: self pointer is NULL", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self_ptr != 0);
        // Assert precondition: buffer must be initialized.
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len == 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: rgba_buffer is empty", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 != 0) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: rgba_buffer length ({d}) is not divisible by 4", .{self.rgba_buffer.len});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len % 4 == 0);
        const expected_size = @as(usize, self.width) * @as(usize, self.height) * 4;
        if (self.rgba_buffer.len != expected_size) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.getBuffer: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_size, self.rgba_buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len == expected_size);
        // Return slice of static buffer: use & to get pointer to array.
        return &self.rgba_buffer;
    }

    /// Present macOS window: draw RGBA buffer to view using NSBitmapImageRep and NSImage.
    /// Why: Simpler than layer-backed views - we create an NSImage from our buffer and draw it.
    /// 
    /// Pointer design (TigerStyle single-level only):
    /// - `self: *Self`: Single pointer to Window struct.
    /// - `self.ns_view`: Single pointer to NSView (nullable).
    /// - `self.rgba_buffer`: Static buffer containing RGBA pixels.
    pub fn present(self: *Self) !void {
        // Assert precondition: view must be initialized.
        if (self.ns_view == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: ns_view is NULL. Call show() first.", .{});
        }
        std.debug.assert(self.ns_view != null);
        std.debug.assert(self.rgba_buffer.len > 0);
        
        const view = self.ns_view.?;
        std.debug.print("[window] Presenting buffer to view at: 0x{x}, buffer size: {d} bytes\n", .{ @intFromPtr(view), self.rgba_buffer.len });
        
        // Create NSBitmapImageRep from RGBA buffer.
        const NSBitmapImageRepClass = c.objc_getClass("NSBitmapImageRep");
        if (NSBitmapImageRepClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSBitmapImageRep class not found", .{});
        }
        const allocSel = c.sel_getUid("alloc");
        if (allocSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: alloc selector not found", .{});
        }
        const bitmapRep_alloc_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSBitmapImageRepClass), allocSel);
        if (bitmapRep_alloc_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSBitmapImageRep alloc returned NULL", .{});
        }
        const bitmapRep_alloc: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(bitmapRep_alloc_opt.?));
        
        // Initialize with bitmap data: initWithBitmapDataPlanes:pixelsWide:pixelsHigh:bitsPerSample:samplesPerPixel:hasAlpha:isPlanar:colorSpaceName:bytesPerRow:bitsPerPixel:
        // We'll use a simpler approach: create CGImage first, then convert to NSImage.
        const cg_image = try createCGImageFromBuffer(&self.rgba_buffer, self.width, self.height);
        defer releaseCGImage(cg_image);
        
        // Create NSImage from CGImage.
        const NSImageClass = c.objc_getClass("NSImage");
        if (NSImageClass == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSImage class not found", .{});
        }
        const nsImage_alloc_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend0(@ptrCast(NSImageClass), allocSel);
        if (nsImage_alloc_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSImage alloc returned NULL", .{});
        }
        const nsImage_alloc: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsImage_alloc_opt.?));
        
        // Initialize NSImage with CGImage: initWithCGImage:size:
        // Note: initWithCGImage:size: takes CGImageRef (pointer) and NSSize (struct by value).
        // We'll use objc_msgSend_wrapper_rect which handles struct-by-value on arm64.
        const initSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithCGImage:size:");
        if (initSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: initWithCGImage:size: selector not found", .{});
        }
        // Create NSSize struct for image size (passed by value on arm64).
        const NSSize = extern struct {
            width: f64,
            height: f64,
        };
        const image_size = NSSize{
            .width = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.width)),
            .height = @as(f64, @floatFromInt(self.height)),
        };
        // Use wrapper_rect which handles struct-by-value: it takes a pointer to the struct.
        // But initWithCGImage:size: takes CGImageRef first, then NSSize.
        // We need a different wrapper. For now, let's try a simpler approach: use NSBitmapImageRep directly.
        // Actually, let's use a C wrapper function for this complex call.
        // For now, let's try using objc_msgSend_wrapper_rect but pass CGImage as first arg.
        // Actually, let's create NSImage differently - use initWithSize: and then lockFocus to draw CGImage.
        const initSizeSel = c.sel_getUid("initWithSize:");
        if (initSizeSel == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: initWithSize: selector not found", .{});
        }
        const nsImage_init_opt = cocoa.objc_msgSend1(@ptrCast(nsImage_alloc), initSizeSel, &image_size);
        if (nsImage_init_opt == null) {
            std.debug.panic("Window.present: NSImage initWithSize: returned NULL", .{});
        }
        const nsImage: *c.objc_object = @ptrCast(@alignCast(nsImage_init_opt.?));
        std.debug.print("[window] Created NSImage at: 0x{x}\n", .{@intFromPtr(nsImage)});

    fn createCGImageFromBuffer(buffer: []const u8, width: u32, height: u32) !*anyopaque {

        const expected_size = @as(usize, width) * @as(usize, height) * 4;
        if (buffer.len != expected_size) {
            std.debug.panic("createCGImageFromBuffer: buffer size mismatch. Expected {d}, got {d}", .{ expected_size, buffer.len });
        }
        std.debug.assert(buffer.len == expected_size);

        const rgb_color_space = cg.CGColorSpaceCreateDeviceRGB();
        if (rgb_color_space == null) {

            null, // info pointer
            buffer.ptr, // data pointer
            buffer.len, // size
            null, // release callback (we manage memory ourselves)

        // Format: RGBA, 8 bits per component, 32 bits per pixel.
        // Note: kCGImageAlphaPremultipliedLast means RGBA format (alpha last).
```
